changes.what: [Fix] Note for upgraders: v0.13.0 fixes a group of memory-safety bugs in the socket-layer context propagation. The header injector no longer acts on a leftover message buffer, which could write a `traceparent` into the middle of a TLS stream and reset the instrumented connection; message-buffer reads are bounded by the mapped data window, so a failed pull no longer copies adjacent kernel memory into span payloads, and sends of 8 KiB or more are captured again. Installs running `presets.contextPropagation` should take this image

findings.title: Drop internal spans in non-critical services (keep errors)
findings.plain: Internal spans describe steps inside one service. In non-critical services they are rarely needed and can make up a large share of each trace.
findings.detail: Services: frontend, load-generator, flagd, email, quote, ad, product-reviews, recommendation.

evidence.text: filter $d.tags['span.kind']:string == 'internal' | groupby $l.serviceName aggregate count() as spans | orderby spans desc
aggregate count() as spans

findings.observedVolume: 370.6K INTERNAL spans/day in non-critical services (17.3% of spans)

savings.basis: Upper bound: all INTERNAL spans in non-critical services (error spans are kept, so slightly less) (17.3% of spans) × 7.36 GB/day of traces, at the customer's blended traces rate over the last 7 complete days (0.250 units/GB, from official tier rates). Assumes average span size.

verifyChecklist: Do engineers use internal spans of these services when investigating?

findings.title: Join multi-line logs into single entries
findings.plain: Stack traces and pretty-printed JSON are split into one log per line. Each fragment is billed and none is useful alone.
findings.detail: Top fragments: "    }", "{", "      ],", "}", "  }", "  },". The fragments are pieces of pretty-printed JSON, so an event starts with a line beginning `{`. In OpenTelemetry this is configured on the filelog receiver, not a processor.

evidence.text: filter length($d.body:string) < 10 | groupby $d.body:string as log_body aggregate count() as occurrence_count, sum(byteLength($d.body:string)) as body_bytes | orderby occurrence_count desc
filter $d.body:string.startsWith('at ') | groupby $l.subsystemname aggregate count() as log_count | orderby log_count desc
aggregate count() as log_count, sum(byteLength($d.body:string)) as body_bytes

savings.basis: Each fragment is a separate record carrying full metadata. Saving ≈ fragments × (average billed bytes per log 1983 B − fragment body), since the merged text is kept, at the customer's blended logs rate over the last 7 complete days (0.651 units/GB, from official tier rates).

verifyChecklist: What does the first line of each log event look like for these services (timestamp format)?

change.summary: Join multi-line events on the filelog receiver

caveats: The regex must match the first line of each event for these services; confirm with a sample before rollout.
Better still: log JSON on a single line in the application.
Shown for reference. Investigate findings cover the same log data, so this estimate is not added to the combined total.
findings.nextStep: Set `multiline.line_start_pattern` on the filelog receiver so each event starts at its first line (timestamp, or `{` for pretty-printed JSON).

findings.title: Remove heavy, unused log attributes
findings.plain: Some attributes are attached to every log but never searched. They add size, and size is what units are charged on.
findings.detail: Measured attribute payload: log.file.path: 91.64 MB/day, log.iostream: 14.96 MB/day, logtag: 5.82 MB/day, time: 28.16 MB/day.

evidence.text: source logs | create search from $d.attributes['log.file.path'] | filter search != null | create byte_length from byteLength(search:string) | aggregate avg(byte_length) as avg_bytes_size, count() as log_count | create gb_usage from ((avg_bytes_size * log_count) / 1000 / 1000 / 1000)

source logs | create search from $d.attributes['log.iostream'] | filter search != null | create byte_length from byteLength(search:string) | aggregate avg(byte_length) as avg_bytes_size, count() as log_count | create gb_usage from ((avg_bytes_size * log_count) / 1000 / 1000 / 1000)

source logs | create search from $d.attributes['logtag'] | filter search != null | create byte_length from byteLength(search:string) | aggregate avg(byte_length) as avg_bytes_size, count() as log_count | create gb_usage from ((avg_bytes_size * log_count) / 1000 / 1000 / 1000)

source logs | create search from $d.attributes['time'] | filter search != null | create byte_length from byteLength(search:string) | aggregate avg(byte_length) as avg_bytes_size, count() as log_count | create gb_usage from ((avg_bytes_size * log_count) / 1000 / 1000 / 1000)

findings.title: ECS: Compact repeated resource blocks with groupbyattrs
findings.plain: Some shippers repeat the full resource header on every batch. Compacting them makes requests smaller and the collector more efficient.
findings.detail: Receivers like Fluent Bit-style forwarders and Prometheus scrapes repeat the resource header on every batch. Pipelines: traces, metrics, logs.
findings.observedVolume: Pipelines without groupbyattrs: traces, metrics, logs

savings.basis: Compaction reduces requests and memory, not ingested units.

verifyChecklist: Is a batch processor present immediately after groupbyattrs in each pipeline?
caveats: Efficiency lever: smaller requests and less memory, not a unit saving.
findings.nextStep: Add groupbyattrs (keys: []) immediately before batch in the listed pipelines.

findings.title: ECS: Add memory_limiter first and batch last in every pipeline
findings.plain: A collector that runs out of memory drops everything during the outage. memory_limiter protects it, and batch sends data efficiently.
findings.detail:
collector/traces: no memory_limiter
collector/metrics: no memory_limiter
collector/metrics: batch is not last
collector/logs: no memory_limiter
findings.observedVolume: collector/traces: no memory_limiter; collector/metrics: no memory_limiter; collector/metrics: batch is not last; collector/logs: no memory_limiter

savings.basis: Stability baseline; prevents data loss during memory pressure.

verifyChecklist: Are memory requests and limits set on the collector pods so limit_percentage is meaningful?

change.snippet:
processors:
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 8192
    timeout: 5s

findings.nextStep: Put memory_limiter first and batch last in every pipeline.

findings.title: Kubernetes: Compress exported data
findings.plain: Compression reduces network egress. It does not change Coralogix units, because units are measured on data size before compression.

savings.basis: Network egress only — not Coralogix units.

verifyChecklist: Is network egress a cost the customer cares about?
caveats: Saves network egress only; Coralogix units are measured before compression.
findings.nextStep: Remove `compression: none` (gzip is the OTLP default) or set zstd.

findings.title: Kubernetes: Set a sensible span metrics cardinality limit
findings.plain: The span metrics connector can cap unique label combinations. Extra ones fold into one overflow series (otel.metric.overflow="true").
findings.detail: spanmetrics: uses deprecated dimensions_cache_size

savings.basis: Safety cap; protects collector memory and storage.

caveats: Fix cardinality upstream first, then set the limit near the steady-state series count. Raising the limit only delays the problem and costs collector memory.
dimensions_cache_size is deprecated in favour of aggregation_cardinality_limit (spanmetricsconnector README).
findings.nextStep: Fix cardinality upstream first, then set aggregation_cardinality_limit near the steady-state series count. New combinations beyond the limit fold into one series with otel.metric.overflow="true".

findings.title: Keep errors and slow traces, sample healthy traffic
findings.plain: Every request creates a trace, and most of them look the same. Tail sampling keeps the traces that explain problems and stores only a small sample of healthy ones.
findings.detail: Policy order: errors (critical services 100%, others 1%), slow traces over 500 ms, then 1% of OK/UNSET. Estimated kept share: 1.0%.

changes.what: [Fix] Note for upgraders: v0.13.0 fixes a group of memory-safety bugs in the socket-layer context propagation. The header injector no longer acts on a leftover message buffer, which could write a `traceparent` into the middle of a TLS stream and reset the instrumented connection; message-buffer reads are bounded by the mapped data window, so a failed pull no longer copies adjacent kernel memory into span payloads, and sends of 8 KiB or more are captured again. Installs running `presets.contextPropagation` should take this image
changes.explanation: Chart release note for upgraders. Check whether it affects your values.

changes.what: [Change] Note for upgraders: `service.name` and `service.namespace` are no longer default metric attributes. They remain resource attributes, so the OTLP metrics this chart exports still carry the service identity and the Coralogix pipeline is unaffected. Prometheus scrapers lose the `service_name` / `service_namespace` labels on application metric series; restore them with `config.data.attributes.extra_group_attributes.app: [service.name, service.namespace]`, or join through `target_info`
changes.explanation: Chart release note for upgraders. Check whether it affects your values.

changes.what: [Change] Note for upgraders: Go runtime metric probes now require the `application_runtime` feature. The `presets.runtimeMetrics` preset already adds it, so a default install keeps Go runtime metrics; installs that configure `metrics.features` by hand must include it
changes.explanation: Chart release note for upgraders. Check whether it affects your values.

changes.what: [Change] Note for upgraders: `error.type` values are unified across spans and metrics, and TCP client/server roles are classified by the local port, which corrects previously swapped roles for same-namespace clients
changes.explanation: Chart release note for upgraders. Check whether it affects your values.

changes.what: [Change] Note for upgraders: `service.peer.name`, `http.request.body.size`, `http.response.body.size` and `obi.http.response.observed` are now opt-in span attributes. The chart's default `config.data.attributes.select.traces.include: ['*']` keeps selecting them; installs that override that selection must include them explicitly, e.g. `service.peer.name` for service-graph generation
changes.explanation: Chart release note for upgraders. Check whether it affects your values.

changes.what: [Change] Note for upgraders: with `metrics.features` including `application` or `application_red`, HTTP duration and body-size metrics now carry `error.type` on failed requests, which recreates the existing series in Prometheus.
